elution_9uL.verdict: 8 uL can be drawn with the p10 tip offset 0.4 mm away from the pellet side, ~0.97 mm from the pellet surface (before the XY positioning stack)
elution_9uL.assumptions: tip end OD 0.8, pellet 0.3 thick, wall 0.25: MEASURE (BR-1 + a bead trial)

pull_off.note: the plate is polypropylene: the magnets pull only on the beads (estimate <= 0.1 mg magnetite-equivalent per well at ~100 T/m). Lift the plate off at <= 10 mm/s and <= 1 m/s^2 so the liquid does not slosh; the pellet stays on the wall by adhesion until resuspended off the magnet

mb1_passive_magnet_block_rev_f.stray_field_limits: bead pelleting needs tens of mT; < 1 mT at a neighbouring plate is harmless; steppers and mechanical (D2F) or optical switches are unaffected below ~1 mT; Earth field 0.05 mT
handling: N52 blocks snap together: handle one at a time, keep loose magnets >= 100 mm apart, wear gloves and glasses
fill the pockets with a non-magnetic (PA/brass) push stick from a jig; mark polarity with a pen before insertion
insert rows in the alternating order: check each with a compass/polarity tester before pressing
keep phones, cards, steel tools and implanted-device wearers away (>= 0.5 m) during assembly
do not drill, heat > 80 C (N52 working limit) or drop (brittle, chips fly)
store and ship the finished MB-1 with a steel keeper plate over the rows
mb1_passive_magnet_block_rev_f.magnet_stays_magnetised_note: N52 max working 80 C: B2 is not next to the thermocycler exhaust; check B2 air temperature at commissioning

sbs_seat.positional_repeatability: +/-0.20 mm for a nominal SBS part; +/-0.33 mm for a part at -0.25 mm (ANSI tolerance); a +0.25 mm part still drops in (0.075 mm per side)
sbs_seat.tc24a_note: existing TC24-A (cad/build.py) reused unchanged as the strip/tube rack; it seats in IN-P with the same play

gripper_corridors.definition: both long sides, y from SBS edge to GRIP_OPEN/2 + finger (52.0 mm from nest centre), full SBS length, z from seat+8 = 13 to MAX_LABWARE_H

assumptions: deck supported on 2040 beams on edge (20 wide, 40 tall) under the 32 mm webs at y = -110, 0, 110 and under the margins at y = +/-225, side beams at x = +/-230; X beams simply supported between side beams
I(2040 strong axis) = 65000 mm^4 assumed; E = 69000 MPa

beam y=110 stops at x=-47 (clear of TC-1 under the bay) and its end sits on a 12 x 20 mm post at x -47..-35 (frame rev B); the 14 mm web at x=-66 between the bay and C2/D2 is no longer over the beam end (see cad/lh1/assembly report, deck_y110_support)

load at the nest centre on the insert; insert = simply supported plate over the window (Timoshenko alpha); 10 % of the load per 14 mm deck web as a point load on a simply supported strip between beam edges; contributions summed (conservative)
deck_deflection.point_20N_at_deck_centre_note: deck centre (0,0) lies on the y=0 web directly over a beam: plate term ~0, value is beam bending
deck_deflection.without_beam_y110_note: if the y=110 beam is simply omitted the 14 mm webs span 205 mm: not acceptable; post or beam required

magnet_module.layout: 6 rows of 7 N52 2x10x20 mm blocks (magnetised through 2 mm), one row in every other column gap (between columns 1-2, 3-4 ... 11-12): every well has one magnet face beside it -> side pellet; rows span wells A-H
magnet_module.pellet_parameter: MAG['pellet_top'] = magnet top above the well bottom when engaged (default 9.0, tune on bench); the lead screw sets engaged height per plate type in firmware

home_sensor.type: slotted optical interrupter (3 mm slot), flag fin on carrier underside

force.stray_note: no ferrous part within 30 mm of the magnets except the two guide rods, which sit symmetrically between rows (net ~0); 5 N allowance covers asymmetry, steel screws and neighbour modules
force.actuator: NEMA17 with integrated T8 lead screw, lead 2 mm, running torque taken as 0.20 N m, efficiency 0.30
force.self_locking: lead angle 4.5 deg < friction angle ~8.5 deg: holds position unpowered

assumptions: room 24 C, block 4 C, under-deck air 25 or 30 C
h = 10 W/m2K on exposed cold Al (convection + radiation)
2 x TEC1-12706 class (Vmax 15.2 V, Imax 6 A, dTmax 66 K), driven at <= 12 V each (2 in series on 24 V)
load x 1.25 margin; 0.15 K/W block-to-cold-face per module; foam EPDM k = 0.04
tube block open (no lid); tubes and reagents add only transient load
thermal_budget.verdict: MARGINAL: a fan-cooled sink inside the 118 x 78 window and 110 mm clearance (~0.6 K/W) holds 4 C only with under-deck air <= ~25 C; with 30 C under-deck air expect ~6-8 C. Remedies in order: duct fresh room air to the fan intake, lid on the tube block, nylon clamp screws, 1 TEC at ~3 A (better COP than 2) or heat pipe to a larger sink outside the window (needs a params change).
thermal_budget.estimated_sink_note: 110 x 70 x 40 fin sink + 60 x 60 x 25 fan within the window: ~0.4-0.6 K/W by typical data; this estimate uses h=30 W/m2K, fin efficiency 0.85, 3.5 L/s
thermal_budget.heating_note: 40 C is easy: TEC reversed, heating COP > 1; limit block to 50 C by firmware and the 60-72 C TCO

cold_block_rev_j.limits: TEC-1166 channel 3.5 A / 18 V (two modules in series: 9 V each)
cold_block_rev_j.answer: YES (rev K sink, theta 0.210 K/W CALCULATED): 4 C held at 25 C ambient (lowest -8.5 C, pull-down 5.7 min) and at 30 C (lowest -4.0 C, pull-down 8.3 min, margin 2.16); with the sink 50 % worse than calculated (0.30 K/W) still 0.4 C at 30 C, 13 min.  MEASURE on the bench rig: sink theta under a 60 W resistor load at the fan's real flow; block temperature, current and voltage at 4 C, 25 and 30 C ambient
assumptions: TEC1-12706 class model (Vmax 15.2 V, Imax 6 A, dTmax 66 K), 0.15 K/W block-to-cold-face per module
sink 0.6 K/W with the 60 mm fan (estimate +/-40 %), sink air = ambient (under-deck air = room)
loaded 12-column strip carrier: exposed top area x 1.6, 96 x 50 uL, carrier 60 g aluminium; 50 % RH
no 1.25 load margin here (thermal_budget keeps it): margin is reported as pumped / load
